transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m having a hard time staying on track. Like, I’ll be working on a dashboard or something, and one Slack notification, or even a song lyric or a random idea for another project, can completely pull me away. Then I realize I’ve lost the thread of what I was supposed to be finishing.
Thinking back, have you noticed this kind of distractibility and trouble staying on task since you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's really only become a problem more recently?

It’s been there since I was little, not just recently. In elementary school, teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets or losing track of the directions. I’d also talk over other kids during group work. At home, my parents would sit next to me for homework because if they didn’t, I’d wander off or start doing something else before I finished.
Besides the distractibility, do you also notice things like feeling physically restless, fidgeting, needing to move around, or blurting things out and interrupting others in conversations?

Yeah, I do notice that. In meetings or portfolio reviews, I’m usually doing something with my hands or moving around—bouncing my leg, clicking a pen, twisting my rings, shifting in my chair. I don’t always realize I’m doing it until someone looks over or I catch myself.
Do these struggles with focus and restlessness cause noticeable problems for you in more than one area of your life right now—for example, both at work and in your personal or home life?

Yeah, it does. It’s not just one setting. I’ve lost a couple small freelance contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly or missed pieces of what I was supposed to deliver. I also missed out on a portfolio competition for similar reasons. And personally, some friends or people I’d collaborate with are kind of hesitant to work with me now, even though they like my ideas, because they’re not sure they can rely on me.
Have you ever had distinct periods—lasting days to weeks—where your mood, energy, or need for sleep changed dramatically, separate from how you feel most of the time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have stressful days or times where I sleep worse, but I haven’t noticed a clear stretch of days or weeks where my mood or energy is dramatically different from my usual.

Do you notice these focus and restlessness issues happening even when you're feeling calm and not anxious, and are you currently using any substances like caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, or recreational drugs regularly?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it out, but yeah, I think it can happen even when I’m not especially anxious. As for substances, I don’t really know what would count as regular use—I don’t have anything specific to mention there.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, lifelong (since elementary school) symptoms of both inattention (distractibility by external stimuli, losing track of tasks, difficulty completing work, disorganization) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (fidgeting, restlessness, interrupting/talking over others, difficulty staying seated/still in meetings). Symptoms began in childhood, are pervasive across multiple settings (work/freelance projects and personal relationships), and cause clear functional impairment (lost contracts, missed competition, strained relationships). No evidence of a manic/hypomanic episode to suggest bipolar disorder, and symptoms occur independent of anxiety, making combined-type ADHD (F90.2) the best fit over inattentive-only (F90.0) or hyperactive-impulsive-only (F90.1) subtypes.
